title: Idempotency keys and idempotent consumers

kcs.statement: The client generates a unique idempotency key per logical operation and resends the same key on every retry; the server stores key → result and returns the stored result for a repeat instead of executing again.

The server must record the idempotency key and perform the side effect in the same transaction, otherwise a crash between them re-opens the duplicate window; stored keys expire after a TTL longer than the client's retry horizon.

An idempotent consumer records each processed message id in the same transaction as the message's business effect and skips ids already recorded; when the effect is external (a card charge, an SMS) and cannot share that transaction, local deduplication alone cannot guarantee it happens once, so the external system must enforce idempotency, for example by accepting an idempotency key.

problem_ideas: Write handle_payment(key, amount, store) that charges once and returns the cached result on repeats
